reviews.text: Big thanks and acknowledgement to Dr. Soto and her team Jayleen, Ashley, Chelsea, and Jo. My min pin Brooklyn needed luxating patella surgery on left rear leg and I was refered to Dr Soto who specializes in this type of procedure for small dogs by one of my neighbors. Three months later and I’m pleased to say the surgery was a success and part of that was due to the fantastic follow-up after care provided by Dr Soto and the entire team:) Blue Pearl pet care is wonderful and they’re passionate and committed to making sure your dog is cared for like they’re own-highly recommend and thanks again to Dr Soto and and entire team-great job!

Dr Soto, Chelsea, Jo, Brando, and Sara took great care of Hud during his surgery and quick recovery.
He is a completely new cat again full of life and energy! Thank you so much!!

This review is for Dr Farrell, she gave us excellent care, was extremely compassionate, attentive, informative empathetic and supportive during an extremely difficult time. She is exemplary and I can not thank her enough for what she helped us navigate.
got some bad news but they were careful and thorough in explaining all our options. very much appreciated!

I will recommend this hospital to anybody who loves their animal. I took my cat Jane here and she had to stay for 5 days for emergency surgery. The love, care and compassion that both of us received during this is something I won’t ever forget. Thank you all so so much for saving my baby and being so thoughtful through that difficult time  5 stars 10/10 thank you!!
All the staff and doctors were so kind & caring to my pet Honey .Excellent service & staff
Unfortunately, I had to go to this hospital two times but everyone I dealt with was so friendly and so helpful and so nice it made a very unpleasant experience a little bit better

This is a difficult review for me to write because I had gotten really good service and treatment for a previous dog and easily spent approximately $16,000 over a year and half period to treat a previous dog suffering from lymphoma.  That dog has since passed.  Enter the new dog.  I brought my new dog in around 10:30pm last night.  He accidentally chewed on some wooden chopsticks.  I know, I need to be more vigilant.  Worried he swallowed a piece, I brought him in for an exam and X-Rays.  $1,451 later and everything seemed to be ok.  Here's what just rubbed me the wrong way:  When they admitted my dog, my dog was scared.  Instead of soliciting my help, the tech drags my dog down the hallway.  I intervene and say, "Let me help." I walked the dog to surgical and he was taken back.  Then, when I was waiting to pick my dog up afterwards, a new tech was dragging my dog, this time with a leash around his throat, and it's clearly choking him.  I was outside, so I ran in to intervene again.  It's 3:23am, I just dropped almost $1,500 and the tech drags my dog by his throat!  At this point, my dog is wearing a cone that the tech says is unnecessary.  So why put it on?! And, she says, "Sorry, I couldn't get his harness on over the cone."  The dog was sedated.  No one thought to put the harness on first and then the unnecessary cone?  I asked to see a supervisor, but she was on lunch and couldn't take 5 minutes to talk to me.  At this point, the place was nearly empty except for another couple admitting their dog.  I explained what I had witnessed to a clerk behind the counter and he said I would have to wait another 20 to 25 minutes to explain what I saw to the supervisor.  No one showed compassion, empathy, and shame for dragging and choking my dog.  Makes me wonder how they treat my dog when I am not looking.  Before BluePearl bought this business, I never saw anything like that. Now, they should be ashamed of themselves.  Do not take your dog here, unless you want it mistreated.

Very disappointing experience

We brought our dog here expecting an emergency visit and were told the wait could be around 3 hours. After waiting about an hour, we were told it could potentially be another 4+ hours. With a sick pet, that was extremely stressful.

Our experience with the receptionist was also disappointing. We were already under a lot of stress, and I felt the communication could have been much more patient and professional.

We were quoted approximately $850 for X-rays, which was far beyond what we were expecting.

We ultimately decided to leave and went about two blocks away to VetNow Animal Urgent Care. We were able to be seen without the same extended wait, and we were quoted around $500 for the visit and X-rays.

I understand emergency hospitals can be busy and that prices can vary depending on the situation. However, based on our experience, the combination of the wait, communication, and cost was not something we were comfortable with.
Kindness of staff, expertise of specialists, transparency of costs all appreciated.  I have such great confidence that my dog cleo is in the best hands
Early Sunday morning emergency handle with such expediency and care. Thank you BluePearl care team – Paula, Malayiah, Carla, Roxy and Dr. Wu!!!

⭐ 1-Star Review — Please Do Your Research

I understand that emergency hospitals can be extremely busy and that more critical cases need to be prioritized. I had sympathy for that and was willing to wait. However, my experience at Trucare was extremely frustrating.

I brought my dog, Bigxby, early in the morning because she was in severe pain and clearly suffering. I called off work because, as a pet parent, you don't think twice when your fur baby is in agony. I expected an emergency hospital to at least evaluate her in a timely manner.

Instead, we waited approximately six hours. We were told several times that we had already been assigned to a veterinarian and would be seen shortly, but hours passed.

When we were finally seen, the consultation lasted about 10 minutes. Bigxby was given pain medication, and an X-ray and bloodwork were recommended. Unfortunately, there was also a lot of confusion afterward about when the tests would be done. I received conflicting information from different staff about whether her X-ray had been taken and repeatedly had to ask for updates.

By the time we left, I was exhausted and frustrated, but most importantly, I still didn't understand what was happening with my dog.

Two days later, Bigxby became paralyzed in her hind legs.

I immediately contacted our primary veterinarian, who had us come in and ultimately referred us for emergency surgery that same day.

That experience eventually led us to another emergency hospital, where the difference in urgency, communication, organization, and care was remarkable.

I am sharing this review because I wish I had researched more before bringing Bigxby here. When your pet is suffering, you don't always think clearly—you just want help as quickly as possible.

Please do your research ahead of time and know where you will take your pet in an emergency. I truly hope other pet parents have a better experience than we did.

If you have need of an emergency vet clinic, I can’t recommend anyone better than TrueCare for Pets/BluePearl Pet Hospital. Our older dog had a seizure at 3:00 AM and rushed to their location. Upon our arrival we were treated to exceptional service and our pet was immediately made a priority. They did an initial exam, and gave us recommendations within minutes. As a pet owner, all you want is to make sure your pet is comfortable, under good care, and you as the owner want to be well informed. All of this was accomplished within minutes of arriving. Unfortunately, the poor guy didn’t recover, so we needed to make the toughest decision to let him cross the rainbow bridge. The entire staff and veterinary crew, were AMAZINGLY SYMPATHETIC TO OUR PAIN, AND REALLY HELPED GUIDE AND COMFORT US THROUGH THE ENTIRE PROCESS.

This was nearly a zero stars/ one star review.  However, my dog received care from Dr. Craig, who was kind, patient, communicative, competent, with good beside manner and deep compassion.  My dog lives and I am very grateful that Dr. Craig saved my dog's life.  My dog was at this hospital for about 28 hours.  Five stars for Dr. Craig.

Prior to Dr. Craig's shift, my dog was seen by Dr. de Anda and it was a horrific, horrific, infuriating experience.  I had little confidence in her ability to attend to and save my dog from a life-threatening situation.  Her communication was awful, cold, and nonsensical.  I was out of the country and desperately calling trusted friends to pull her out of this hospital, as I had zero confidence in Dr. de Anda's willingness and blasé attitude to save my dog's life.  Zero star review for Dr. de Anda.

This all averages out to 3 stars for the hospital.  The assistants were good and communicative, and for that, the hospital gets one more star for a 4 star review.

Bottom line- If Dr. Craig is here, feel confident that your animal will be getting attentive care and she will communicate with you in a humane manner that allows you to make well-informed decisions for your animal's care. Avoid Dr. de Anda!

DO NOT GO HERE!! If your dog refuses to eat and has bloody stool remember to do a Fecal test first and foremost, Coccidia is a common virus found in dirty water and food on the street, (especially if you have a lab).
TrueCare preys on your dog and your fears.
They bypassed a simple consultation and advised us immediate action is necessary and when a simple fecal tests showed a common virus. Later we checked on google and the AI results gave us all of the symptoms our dog had from Coccidia, you’re telling me a professional doctor knows less than google AI???!!
I can’t believe I’m giving a 1 star, this deserves less

::update::
After our Rottweiler decided to try and catch a raccoon and got bit, they took her in right away, triaged her to determine she wasn't in danger, and then saw and treated her.. This place is a fantastic emergency vet, especially in the middle of the night.. I can't say enough good things about them..

After a previous negative experience. True care was the closest emergency vet for my dying cat. They treated him immediately, stabilized him as much as they could to allow my wife and I to say goodbye. We had no clue he was so sick. The care we received from true care was immediate, professional, and treated my cat with priority, dignity, and compassion. They made him comfortable in his last moments, and allowed us to spend as much time as we needed to say goodbye.. It's only been 24 hours. This happened yesterday on 10/16/25. There is a reason emergency vet care is pricey, and that became fully evident yesterday.. I would have paid any price to save my car, but unfortunately there was no cure or fix.. RIP Ash! You were the most loving, softest, and loyal kitty. You will be missed forever.
Thank you True Care for everything you did. It helped make a devastating day, a little better!

My cat ate a string on a Saturday and I brought him to TrueCare knowing it could become life-threatening if it passed into his intestines. The staff responded urgently and brought him back for examination right away. Dr. Sibrian recommended inducing vomiting and was able to retrieve the entire string. I was in and out in about an hour, and everyone I spoke with was very friendly. Highly recommended!

Thank you so much to this incredible team. I took my elderly dog on a hike that she’s done before, but on this given day, her body didn’t do as well as usual, and I took her straight to this location on our way home to check for heat stroke or any issues. Everyone on the team, including Carla, Ryan, Clarissa, Roxy, Misael, and Malayiah were so kind during what was a very stressful situation for me. My girl was in such good hands, and assured me she was alright. The warmth and quick to act energy of this team is sooo appreciated and we will be back if we ever need anything!!

I took my dog in with a mass in his anal gland. Saw the doctor, and she was able to get the cytology to find that it was in fact a carcinoma. We can schedule surgery for last Tuesday. I dropped my pup off, scared to death and left him there for his CT scan and surgery. Both would be under anesthesia. Two hours later I got a call that the “surgery machine” was broken and that I needed to come pick him up because it might be next week before they could get it fixed and they would give me a call when they could. I asked exactly what a surgery machine is. Apparently, it was the anesthesia machine. I went to pick up my dog waited 15 minutes for him to be brought out and the lady again told me that maybe they would be able to give me a call next week and shrugged. I asked to see the Doctor who didn’t come out, although she obviously wasn’t in surgery, if no surgery could be performed, but her nurse did. It was explained to me that it might not even be next week. It could take weeks to get one of these machines fixed, and I think that’s a reflection of this hospital. No reputable emergency room would work with a vendor who takes a few weeks to fix an anesthesia machine. They only have two machines. One in each OR. My fear was that had something happen once he was already under, he would’ve been lost. There is no Plan B as far as machines go. Maybe they would just administer IV propofol and pray. As a burn survivor, I’ve had a lot of surgeries. The anesthesiologist is the most important guy in the room. It didn’t sit right in my spirit and I told him that I wanted to refund and then I was going elsewhere. They had no interest in the fact that my dog has cancer that could be spreading while they’re wasting my time. I went to VCA the next day met with an amazing surgeon and got scheduled for next week. That surgeon even scheduled me on a day off because otherwise it would’ve taken a few weeks to get my dog in. I had just paid true care $7,752 that morning and I asked them to refund it immediately. They did nothing until I called the next day. They clearly stated that they hadn’t issued the refund the day before which would’ve gotten the money back in my account quickly rather than a 5-7 day wait. I canceled my service before they even batched the payments for the day, and if they had only clicked one button.. But they don’t care about your money or your pet. I wouldn’t recommend taking your cockroach here. Other people were being turned away, whose animals needed radiation, etc. being told that the anesthesia machine was down. I did learn that true care is apparently the bargain base because the surgery cost several thousand more at the real animal hospital. I hope your staff at least learns empathy.
paula was very compassionate in a very vulnerable time, my family and i appreciate her efforts in making saying goodbye to our family dog easier
Very attentive, patient and communicative. They’ve been great all around for me and my dog.

Went for internal medicine. Have had a few interactions at this point. Care is ok. Prices are high but it’s a 24/7 hospital so some of that is expected. But monetization feels like their primary ethos. Everything is transactional, price transparency doesn’t exist. If you have a choice do yourself a favor and go somewhere else.

We brought our dog for vomiting and diarrhea August 1st and saw Dr Craig.  As a physician, I have medical knowledge to assess a dog’s problem and the work up and treatment being presented.  Because gastrointestinal issues are the most common issue presenting to a vet, the various causes are numerous but thankfully usually not serious.  The work up was mostly reasonable with a few exceptions.  I don’t believe a venous blood gas was warranted nor a screening abdominal ultrasound as abdominal X-rays were taken. A formal X-ray reading by a radiologist for 3 views was $170 and I think for simple X-rays that a Emergency vets reading should suffice and referred out only if there’s a question about the X-ray.  We were told a stool sample would be sent out but upon discharge we were told it wasn’t and they wanted us to collect a sample at home and bring it back. My vet could always get a sample if needed, so that is a problem.  Lastly, one blood test run was a serum cortisol level to check for Addison’s disease of the adrenal glands and it was run in-house on their machine and it came back borderline low measuring 1.34 and we were given discharge instructions that we should have anACTH test done later to be sure my dog didn’t have early Addisons disease which is a serious disease.  Our vet ran the test which showed an initial cortisol level of 8.1 from an outside lab which is normal. In my mind, there should not be such a great difference in levels and I seriously think that their in-house machine needs to be inspected and checked to be working correctly and I plan to call them to do just that.  In summary, my dog is fine and the stool test and ACTH test are both normal with no clear diagnosis found.  Although everyone was very nice at Trucare, in the future I will be going to other Emergency centers. FYI- Trucare has been bought out, they don’t have an MRI machine onsite which is essential in many true emergencies nor do they have the medical specialists like a neurosurgeon etc .  As a retired Emergency Doctor, having critical specialists is vital for a good outcome in many cases.

I should have read the reviews before I came. Just like others have stated....the focus is money. They rush the animal to the backroom with no explanation and they start procedures without telling you the cost. Very unfriendly staff and you never see the actual doctor. Finally I asked what the cost is and it was 3 times as much as other places (I called around today). Their explanation was that it's higher because it's an emergency.

I was there for more than 3 hours for something that should have taken far less. Again, very unfriendly staff with very bad communication skills. And I DID NOT SEE THE DOCTOR ONE TIME.

The focus here is purely money.

Good luck!

Dr Emily Farrell was so kind and patient. Her calmness was so helpful since I tend to overthink when it comes to my fur babies. And the team was super sweet to my Bandit. I’m so glad we took him there for the urgent care we needed 🙏💕 …

I’ve been here on at least 5 different occasions over the years and it’s always been a positive experience. Everyone is always very thorough, kind, patient and attentive. My last visit, I was particularly impressed and felt compelled to write this review.

My dog was in distress & I was afraid she could have ingested poison. I called from the car and asked them to meet me at the back door, to help carry her inside. There was absolutely no waiting, or needing payment before taking her from me. Luckily she wasn’t poisoned, in all likelihood she ate a 7oh gummy & ended up needing to be hospitalized for two days.

They stayed in communication by phone and text throughout and even sent a few photo updates. I really appreciated that they asked me to come in and spend time with her twice, to give my own assessment. They wanted to make sure that her persistent agitation and distress wasn’t just from being in the hospital (which it wasn’t).

It became clear to me on multiple occasions, that they were trying to be conservative to help save on expenses. I’ve had plenty of experiences elsewhere, where they start by pushing for the higher end of the care spectrum and price range.

Instead of keeping her in a crate the whole time, they let her visit with them in their back office, resting with blankets and listening to soothing music, to help calm her. I really feel they went above and beyond to give her additional needed TLC and not just medical treatment.

During one of my visits with her, the vet took the time to walk around outside with us, so we could properly assess her status together. My girl voluntarily cut the walk short, made a beeline back to the hospital and was happy to leave me and return to the treatment area. She obviously felt very safe and happy there.

When it came time to go home, instead of automatically handing me meds with a bill, they pointed me towards Amazon, which saved me $65. No body wants to have to deal with hospitals and huge vet bills, but I’m very grateful to have True Care nearby if I need them!😅💖🙏🏼

I cannot say enough wonderful things about my experience at TrueCare for Pets today. From the moment we arrived, every member of the staff was kind, compassionate, efficient, and genuinely caring. During such a frightening time, everyone treated both me and my dog, Cooper, with patience and kindness.

Dr. Andrea Armour was truly exceptional. She was incredibly thorough, knowledgeable, and compassionate. She took the time to answer every one of my questions—and even addressed many of the concerns I hadn’t thought to ask yet. I never felt rushed. She explained everything clearly, discussed the possible causes of Cooper’s condition, and made sure I understood the plan moving forward.

What touched me most was her genuine compassion. At one point, she sat on the floor with Cooper and me, making an already stressful experience feel so much less overwhelming. That simple act spoke volumes about the kind of veterinarian she is. Her kindness, empathy, and dedication to both her patients and their families are truly extraordinary.

As a registered nurse, I especially appreciate healthcare professionals who combine clinical excellence with heartfelt compassion, and Dr. Armour exemplifies both. I am deeply grateful for the outstanding care Cooper received and would recommend TrueCare for Pets without hesitation. Thank you to Dr. Andrea Armour and the entire team for treating us with such exceptional professionalism, compassion, and kindness. You made one of the most stressful days imaginable much easier, and I will never forget it.

We brought our dog, Buster, to Blue Pearl Emergency care after he experienced a seizure late at night when our regular vet was unavailable. From the moment we called, to the time we arrived, the staff and Veterinarians were caring, professional, and timely with their exam and treatment. He was seen immediately because of his age and condition, and Dr. Lowdermilk explained what she thought might be causing the seizures and gave us a full range of options for tests that could be run to see what was happening. At no time were we pressured into having them keep him overnight, perform any tests, or follow any specific plan. They simply gave us a list of options and prices and let us decide. Everyone there was extremely kind and caring and tried their best to make a horrible situation better.   Having a visit to an emergency vet is always a stressful situation, but I would unconditionally recommend them as the place to take your pet should it ever happen to you.

Our sweet little Fred swallowed a hair tie and it became a dire situation over the weekend, leaving my wife and I traumatized. The team at TrueCare were really wonderful to us. They managed expectations well and delivered realistic expectations with kindness. Fortunately, the operation was a success, and our little guy is on the road to recovery. We will be taking him back this Sunday, two weeks after the operation, to have his sutures removed.
Special shoutout to Dr Avenick, who performed the procedure, and who was very thorough in discussing the steps and options along the way.
DA Veyda was also absolutely incredible to us! She recognized the emotions we were going through and she clearly cared about our little guy’s wellbeing. She made us feel very comforted and reassured and we have been very touched by her understanding, care and kindness.
I believe Tech Jasson is also on their team, plus Megan, Fatima and Carla. Everyone has been very communicative and understanding and we deeply appreciate everyone’s support during this difficult couple of weeks!

I don't usually post reviews but I am taking the time to give a shout out to Paula and Dr Avernick. They were great. Paula took her time to explain the estimate and was beyond patient with all the questions we had. Dr Avernick was professional and helped my baby feel better.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We are so grateful to Dr. Craig and the entire team at True Care Vet for the exceptional care they provided during our Australian Shepherd’s recent emergency visit for cluster seizures. From the moment we arrived, everyone was compassionate, attentive, and professional during such a frightening time.

Dr. Craig took the time to thoroughly evaluate our dog, explain everything clearly, and answer all of our questions with patience and kindness. The staff kept us informed throughout his stay and treated him with so much care and compassion, which gave us peace of mind when we needed it most.

We truly appreciate the dedication and expertise of everyone at True Care Vet. Thank you for taking such wonderful care of our beloved dog. We highly recommend True Care Vet to anyone looking for an emergency veterinary team that genuinely cares.
This place is magical. Every single person that works there is nicer than the next. They saved my Zelda’s life and I can’t thank them enough for their kindness along the way.

STAY AWAY!

I was shocked by this experience. A friend's dog developed swelling inside his mouth and became ill. Before any definitive diagnosis or treatment, my friend was presented with an estimate of more than $12,000, which did not even include the surgery that might ultimately be required.

I understand that emergency veterinary care is expensive and that advanced imaging such as CT scans can be medically appropriate. What was missing was a clear explanation of why less expensive diagnostic options were not appropriate first, or any meaningful discussion about prioritizing tests based on medical necessity and financial limitations.

The most upsetting part was the hospital's insistence on payment before moving forward. The owner was out of the country and unreachable, so staff repeatedly contacted me asking if I would pay on his behalf. I explained that my credit card had a limit and could only cover part of the estimate. Instead of working with us, they immediately sent me an invoice for the maximum amount I said my card would allow. We were also told that because the owner could not be reached, they could not proceed with the recommended care.

Pet owners facing a medical emergency with their pet deserve transparency, compassion, and clear communication, not to feel like the first priority is securing payment.

In my opinion, this hospital relied heavily on "policy" while showing very little flexibility or empathy during an incredibly stressful situation. Finances were prioritized over helping a ill animal.

In the end, it was 8K to determine it was an abscess. Go figure.
Wonderful! Took my Frenchie in and they gave her such good care. Dr Mitra sat and answered my questions, and the support staff was efficient and also very caring. Highly recommend!

I can not say enough good things about our experience with True Care.  Our golden retriever developed a cancerous tumor in his nose.  After multiple consults (as ridiculous as it sounds, even in other states), we determined that True Care had the best treatment plan.  They quickly got us in for surgery.  Everyone we spoke to, whether in person or on the phone, was professional, friendly and kind.  However, what has stood out the most is their communication.  From techs, to the surgeon, from phone calls to text messages to emails to pictures, we were kept up to date on every single step.  Any concerns I had were immediately responded to with a plan in place.  Our dog is doing very well and should be able to live out his life cancer free thanks to True Care and Dr. Tallant.
Dr. Chaplow and team was so sweet and attentive to my baby Jody. Dr. Chaplow explained the options and helped me make the right decision Jody. Thank you! 💜 …

I brought my cat here after he was bleeding from the nose and had been choking earlier. I was extremely worried and expected this to be treated seriously, but the staff was very rude and kept telling me to wait. They would not allow me to stay with my cat, and I ended up waiting around 4 hours with no real help or answers.

What upset me the most is that other people were taken before us while I was told my cat’s situation was “not an emergency.” My cat was bleeding from the nose — how is that not an emergency?

I left feeling like they did not care at all about my cat or the seriousness of the situation. I would not recommend this place to anyone who truly cares about their pet. Please do not come here. In my opinion, this facility should not be in business if this is how they treat animals and worried pet owners.

I had very positive experiences at TrueCare a few years ago, dealing with a dog who was dying from Hemangiosarcoma.  This was a happier, but just as professional, visit.  My bonehead chews and eats everything, and was suffering gastrointestinal problems, and Dr. Norfeldt, Sara, Ryan, Shelsie, and Autumn all were completely wonderful with him and me.   Nobody is happy about going to an emergency room, especially for a pet, but the people here make it as pleasant and painless as imaginable.

I brought my dog, Sugar, to the ER after she collapsed on our front lawn. I was obviously terrified. The vet team at True Care (Studio City/LA) were unbelievably calm and were able to stabilize her. They accurately assessed her needs and identified the likely cause of the collapse and the necessary course of treatment. I am so thankful that they saved my little fur baby. Without a doubt, I would recommend this hospital to any dog or animal owner. The staff is top notch and the doctors are exceptionally trained, loving, and professional. Thank you for taking such great care of Sugar. We are so grateful.

My big and fluffy 15 years old cat suddenly got sick at about 8:00 P.M. on Friday, and I started calling vet clinics like crazy, realizing that TrueCare was the only Clinic open at that time in my area. Being very stressed out (as he did not want to sit in a carrier), I finally was able to bring him in. From the very moment I walked in, I met only nice, polite, friendly and caring people in this Hospital, people who truly love animals.  I appreciate professional service provided by the Dr. Peter Norfeldt and the whole Team working at that time. Thank you, guys, so much for your help! I highly recommend this Emergency Vet Hospital.

In cannot say enough wonderful things about TrueCare for Pets and Dr. Louderback.

Going through a serious illness with a beloved dog is one of the most difficult experiences a pet owner can face, and Dr. Louderback has been an incredible source of support, compassion, and guidance every step of the way. She has consistently taken the time to thoroughly explain everything, answer my questions with patience, and ensure I felt informed and supported during every decision regarding my dog, Sativa’s care.

What has meant the most is the genuine kindness and compassion she has shown throughout this journey. Even today, she personally checked in to see how Sativa was doing before her scheduled amputation tomorrow. That level of care and dedication goes far beyond what I would ever expect and speaks volumes about the type of veterinarian and person she is.

The entire team at TrueCare for Pets has been professional, caring, and attentive, but Dr. Louderback has made an especially profound impact during one of the most challenging times of my life. I am deeply grateful for all of the care, time, support, and empathy she has given both Sativa and me.

If you’re looking for a veterinary team that truly cares about their patients and the people who love them, I highly recommend TrueCare for Pets and Dr. Louderback. They have my heartfelt gratitude and highest recommendation.

I had to rush my dog to the Vet on an emergency bases, and Peter was amazing. I had taken my sweet baby boy to another vet earlier that day and did not get any assistance after being there for two hours leaving not knowing what was wrong with him. I took him home and his symptoms worsen. I took him into TrueCare at 10 pm and Peter saved my dogs life. I'm so thankful for Peter if it wasn't for him and boy wouldn't be here today.

My cat Simon got badly injured. He’s very old and it was clear he wasn’t going to make it. I took him to TrueCare and the staff was calm, helpful, efficient and caring. They took him in right away. The doctor was especially amazing with us in Simons final moments. You guys are awesome. Thank you for your help and service today. ♥️

This was our first experience with TrueCare for Pets. Our lab is having some intestinal issues and our regular vet referred us to TrueCare to get an expert opinion. From making the appointment to check in to payment, everything was handled easily through text or online. Everyone we interacted with on the staff was very friendly and helpful. We saw Dr. Chaplow, who is just AMAZING! She put us at ease right away, and she explained everything in a way that was easily understandable. Bringing your fur baby to the vet is usually a very stressful experience - thank you TrueCare for taking such good care of us. I would definitely recommend!
Everyone is so nice. My dog Bubba loves to visit.
Horrible place that preys on people’s hopes and fears for the wellbeing of their animals. If you care about your pets and your pocketbook, steer clear of this horrible place.

Went in today with my cat for urgent care, and I absolutely adored all the staff. Everyone here is so caring and nice and it makes me sad to see such a low rating for this place!!! My cat is very bad at the vet because of anxiety and I could tell they were taking their time with him and kept his stress in mind.
The waiting room is also extremely comfy as well and they have free water and coffee!!!
Excellent care, empathy and warmth.  Took great care of our dog and us!  Highly recommend.

Excellent service all around. From the front desk arrival to Dr. Chaplow’s assistants, everyone was friendly caring & efficient. Dr Chaplow is extraordinary. From her detailed understanding & explanation of my dogs illness to the further details provided on the options for treatment after test results, she couldn’t have been more thorough. If only my personal medical professionals were this thorough!

When our cat Teddy got sick just before his first birthday in May 2021, we really thought he wasn't going to make it. My husband took him from the urgent care directly to True Care for treatment for anemia with an unknown cause. Teddy was cared for by Dr. Chaplow and the team and after a few days he was able to come home. Ever since, we have seen Dr. Chaplow for all of Teddy's checkups. She has been so attentive and her staff is amazing, even though he is quite skittish! We always trust Dr. Chaplow to check Teddy's levels and provide the right steroid dose for him. I am so happy to say that Teddy is 6 years old now and is absolutely thriving under her care. Thank you, Dr. Chaplow and team! We love you guys and we appreciate everything you do for our little man Ted!!
They just want money! The estimate for my dog to stay overnight was $5,000. Scammers!

This place deserves all the 🌟 stars after having to euthanize my mama pup they helped me save her liters lives. They wouldn't latch on to the bottle as I'm sure they felt the loss of their mama and my grief. It took one phone call and one car ride they stepped in and the entire staff worked to save the day. When I first arrived, I was immediately told they were going to induce vomiting and was presented with a $600 estimate before I had even spoken with Poison Control. I had to ask whether we should wait to confirm with Poison Control first, especially since there are certain rodenticides where inducing vomiting is not recommended. Shortly after, they came back and said we would wait — which made me question why the initial rush and large estimate were presented without that confirmation.

After Poison Control determined that, based on my dog’s weight and the suspected amount ingested, no emergency treatment was required, we still waited nearly two additional hours just to be discharged. I was not the only person in the lobby expressing concerns about excessive wait times. For an emergency facility, the process felt extremely slow and disorganized.

Additionally, I was prescribed Vitamin K1 (50 mg) and was advised it would be cheaper to obtain it from places like CVS, Walgreens, or Costco. I spent hours calling and driving around to multiple pharmacies only to find that none of them carried it. When I called the clinic for guidance, one staff member told me I would “just have to call around.” Another staff member later admitted that those pharmacies typically do not carry it. This resulted in wasted time, gas, and unnecessary stress, when I could have simply purchased the medication from the clinic the night before.

Lastly, I experienced unprofessional communication at the front desk. When I asked for confirmation that the dosage provided was correct, I was told it was “probably due to her weight.” When I asked for clear confirmation, I was met with attitude rather than reassurance. In a situation involving possible poisoning, clarity and professionalism are critical.

I understand emergency veterinary care is expensive, and I do not dispute being quoted prices. However, the communication, wait times, and inconsistent information made an already stressful situation much harder than it needed to be.

If you love your pet and don’t want to be financially and emotionally drained, think twice before coming here.
I brought my 10-month-old puppy in because he was sick, low-energy, and had a fever. From the moment we arrived, the whole operation felt like a rehearsed sales routine rather than a place focused on helping animals.

They start with a very sweet staff member outside who reassures you, tells you comforting stories, and makes you feel like you’re in “the best hands.” Then reality kicks in. Once they take your dog, you’re suddenly told you must pay before anything else continues. After nearly an hour, I was already charged almost $300 just for the visit, and they ran tests they previously said they wouldn’t. I paid because I wanted my dog helped.

Then came hours of waiting. More than 2.5 hours later, the doctor finally appeared, smiled, asked a few quick questions, wrote a few notes — then disappeared. Five minutes later a different staff member came back with a massive estimate full of outrageous charges. And that’s the pattern:
You barely see the doctor unless it’s tied directly to a payment.
When I explained we were financially tight and asked if there was ANY compassion or discount, the response was basically, “Well… how much can you afford?” Not “Let’s help your dog,” but “How much money can we get from you?” After I was told someone “the other night didn’t even get charged,” suddenly “the doctor said no” when asked if they could help us at all.

By the end of the night, I had already paid close to $2,000. The doctor finally comes back and says:
•	Good news: bloodwork doesn’t show anything major.
•	Frustrating news: they don’t know why he’s sick.
He gives antibiotics and tells me “come back in 48 hours if he’s not better” and reassures me it won’t be the same cost — again, everything wrapped in money talk.

The next morning, my dog’s throat was swollen. I rushed back, expecting urgent care and concern. Instead, I was treated like I had never been there before and the entire expensive process was starting all over again. I waited hours with a sick puppy, with zero updates, zero concern, and zero urgency. No doctor. No nurse. No follow-up. After two hours of being ignored, I left. Hours later — still no call, no check-in, no acknowledgment that my dog was even there earlier.

This place is organized around extracting money first and treating pets second. It feels corporate, cold, and profit-driven, no matter how friendly the smiles are at the beginning. When your dog is sick, you are vulnerable — and this place fully takes advantage of that.

I’m sharing this so other pet owners don’t have to go through what I did. There ARE better emergency hospitals nearby that actually care, are more reasonably priced, and don’t run you through a money machine while your pet suffers.

I will be pursuing this further and requesting a refund. What they’re doing to stressed, emotional pet owners is unacceptable.

never in my life have i ever been compelled enough to leave a bad review for an establishment, as i always thought it to be petty. but after taking my dog to true care, my experience was so beyond horrific that if i could help even one animal with my review, it’s worth the effort to share my story.

i’d like to preface by saying i’ve been here before on a non emergency occasion for my dog, she needed to see a liver specialist a year or two ago and got prescribed medication here. for routine visits, true care has been fine for me, which is the only reason why i won’t give it one star. emergency visits here, however, is an entirely different ordeal

around two weeks ago, my dog suddenly got sick with a strange and aggressive esophagus infection. we didn’t notice she was sick until wednesday night, so we took her to her primary doctor thursday to get x-rays and bloodwork done in an effort to figure out the cause. by the time friday rolled around, she was starting to appear lethargic and, at one point, unresponsive. i called off of work, grabbed her and ran into my car, and drove an hour and a half to true care, which is where our vet referred her to because they had specialists on site.

i run in, tears streaming down my face, and tell the front desk my dog is unresponsive. they take her to a room right away. but then they tell me that because she’s technically not 100% unresponsive (her eyes are open, she’s conscious, she’s a cause for concern but nothing major), priority will be given to other animals unless her condition worsens. so i figured if they said it’s not an emergency, maybe it’s some random infection, and she’ll be fine with some antibiotics they’ll prescribe her.

i wait for over SIX HOURS in a waiting room, while they keep her in an oxygen tank with NO bloodwork done, NO x-rays, NO doctor to see her. finally when night time rolls around, a doctor does a general inspection and tells me there’s nothing they can do because she’s too far gone, and tells us they need to euthanize. they chalked it up to old age. while i understand my dog is older, and they are not responsible for my dog being sick (for all i know, maybe there really was nothing that could’ve been done), if her condition was so dire, it is absolutely unacceptable that it took 6 hours for someone to even look at her. especially considering the fact that this is a top dollar EMERGENCY vet. when i pressed them on this, their excuse was that they were understaffed. why are you understaffed at an emergency vet?? a few hours could make a difference between a life saved and a life lost! i also specifically brought her to true care so she could see an esophagus internist, since they said over the phone before i got there that they have one in-clinic, yet they were nowhere to be found when i got there.

the doctor sees i’m clearly distraught and recommends to do a full panel bloodwork and additional x-rays (i already did x-rays that same day at her primary doctor, but they claimed the x-rays were blurry and should be redone) before making a final diagnosis, to which i accept. they were able to get a bit of blood, but at this stage in her sickness, her blood was too thick to draw, so we never fully did the bloodwork, and we ended up having to euthanize my dog.

a few days after the incident, i’m still in shock at how poorly my dog was treated during her last days, then i remember i paid like $600 for a full blood panel that was never able to be completed. so i call and ask for a partial refund, they said they’ll get back to me — they don’t. i call THREE MORE TIMES after that, over the span of the last two weeks, they keep saying they’ll contact management and call back, yet i’ve reviewed no word of my refund request.

i don’t think i’ve ever been treated more poorly in my life by customer service. to anyone reading this that is considering different emergency hospitals to go to, my vet had also recommended and put in a good word for access emergency vet in san fernando, i’ll forever regret not taking her there instead. thanks for reading.

He needed a feeding tube and a CT scan. The surgeon Dr. Tennant who did all these things called me a few times with updates. She made me feel more relieved and relaxed than I had for three days. They texted me a few times through the night and even sent me a video. When I went to pick up my kitty, everybody was great. So, I must say that from the second we got there until the time we left, they treated us and our kitty so warmly and professionally. Also, they really know what they are doing medically.
So, we just want to say Thank you so much TrueCare

No one ever wants to have to take their pet to an emergency vet, but should the unfortunate occasion arise, TrueCare is absolutely the place to go. The staff is kind, informative, and caring. The facilities are clean and welcoming. Obviously they cannot control the flow of various emergencies that may come in on any given day, so wait times surely fluctuate especially if your animal is (fortunately) deemed stable, they nevertheless keep you well-apprised of the status. Should you need to, this is the place to bring your pet in an emergency and/or after-hours situation!

Absolutely abysmal veterinarian office. Completely negligent of the care and well-being of animals. This place should not be in business. I will drive all the way to another vet, with incredible care, in Orange County, before I’d drive two blocks to this office.

I brought my cat in late tonight, very worried about him, and the team was so kind and compassionate. Because it was a possible life threatening emergency, they saw him right away. The doctor was so kind, reassured me, answered all of my questions, and sent me home feeling much better. I’m so grateful for their care and the kindness they showed me and my cat. Thank you ❤️

Caring for your pet is our top priority, and we always want to ensure you feel valued every step of the way. If there’s anything we could have done differently to make your visit better, we’d truly appreciate your insight. We’re always here to listen.

This review is long overdue.  Last August I brought home a precious 8 week old Scottie puppy from Nevada. Within 3 days, he wasn’t eating, was vomiting and shrinking before my eyes and lost all energy. I took him to True Care where they tested him for parvovirus upon arrival, and it came back positive. Little did I know what an emotional roller coaster and fight my little baby and I would endure for 2 weeks. 1 year later I’m blessed to have my Hugo with me due to the incredible care and efforts by Dr Beymer and team. Every day it was touch and go with terrible news, then hope, then, no hope, and Dr Beymer could not have been more caring and supportive with each decision we made for his care. This  included blood transfusions from a special canine donor, Wanda, who belonged to an employee there. With prayers and the care from the team at True Care, this little man is thriving and playing with his big sis:)

At 2:18 AM, I rushed into this clinic as a Rover dog sitter with a senior dog. He was vomiting, refusing to drink or eat, peeing on the floor, with clear signs of pain. Despite being transparent that this wasn’t my dog, the staff only checked vitals, handed him back, and left us waiting for an hour only to tell us, ‘We can’t provide care without owner’s permission and upfront payment.’ No ultrasound. No bloodwork. Not even pain relief or IV fluids to stabilize him. Their ‘policy’ overrode their oath to ‘do no harm.’

I found another vet ER, and they discovered his gallbladder was about to rupture. It was surgical emergency. This clinic’s refusal to act almost killed him. If you’re a petsitter or owner in crisis, BEWARE! This place will prioritize paperwork over saving lives. Shameful.

I recently had to rush my senior dog of 16 years to receive cpr unfortunately he did not make it but the staff was so reminds and caring I did not have the funds available to cover expenses they helped me out with a discount and let me pay them back when I have the funds available I truly appreciate every staff that helped with my baby boy thank you guys so much for everything you do you guys really helped me so much you have no idea how much it means to me I highly recommend you guys to take your pets here in case of an emergency 🙏❤️

I was out of the country, sadly my sister and son had to handle a very tragic medical emergency to help my beloved pet Rosie Staffordshire Terrier/ Boxer mix . She now rests in heaven do to old age and multiple ailments. Dr. Farrow was compassionate and very understanding of grieving pet owners . Always do a pre search of an emergency facility PRIOR to having to go to one, just throwing this out there.
Note: Five stars was not given because I was not there to witness firsthand.

From the moment we got there, they were wonderful and empathetic. They brought my 14yo Bully in on a gurney. They moved her from last in the first priority. Unfortunately it was fatal news. The Vet spent a long time with us weight the options and she was above and beyond kind and patient. They let us stay with her in a private room as long as we needed. It was the best and worst vet experience I have ever had. I HIGHLY recommend the care here.

I brought my 11 yr old Puggle to TC for emergency Surgery to remove Spleen & tumor. I was referred by 24 hr emergency pet care on Moorpark in T.O. after paying them $2200.00 we were advised that my dog was in good condition for surgery. They claim to have called other nearby locations, but none could take him TC was our only option. My dog had a cancerous tumor, but I was told  o cancer was evident in any other vital organs. What I was not ready or prepared for, was a surgery & overnight care bill exceeding $16,000. Yes you read that Right!! I know I had the option to euthanize, but I had extreme high hopes to give him a chance for longer life. I was under extreme duress & sadness. I am 75 with limited income. I really wonder where the companion is, why in heavens name would a Vet Hospital charge people such exorbitant fees. I feel that I was severely taken advantage of. A return consultantation for follow up, cost me additional $250!!! I should have been advised it was not included. In that consultation, I was told if we chose to give Chemo, ($10,000 for first treatment) the dog could live 9 to 12 months. Without it, 1 to 3 months. We could NOT afford it. I had to borrow the $18k for care already given, so further debt was not an option. We've been treating the dog Holistically,. July 29th was exactly 3 months since surgery. He has been very active, alert,  playful, good appetite and basically doing very well. We are praying it continues.  While the staff  & care was outstanding, I am still loosing sleep about the extreme over pricing.

This was a terrible experience!! I brought my dog who is 17 years old and was  vomiting. Once there her vitals were fine after i waited two and a half hours! They then wanted to do Xray’s in stomach blood work and esophagus even though i just had blood work done less then a week ago! They wanted to charge me $1300 even though she was stable and i told them i would bring her to my own vet!! They made me sign AMA forms and wouldn’t release my dog until i paid 300 after a 2 and a half hour wait !  All in Red warning section ! This place is a scam and all about the money! They take advantage of the fact that as a pet owner you are in Crisis! I would avoid if Possible !!!

honestly very off-putting business practice, my primary vet suggested coming here for a urinary blockage with my cat, but if I could go back in time and take my cat somewhere else I would. DO NOT COME HERE unless you have money to burn and say yes to everything they want to bill you for. They attempted to overcharge me 3 times and was left with maybe $70 of veterinary cat food and gabapentin ... why was this $4000? DO NOT COME HERE THEY WILL SCAM YOU BEYOND BELIEF

This hospital provided top care for our pet. They got her in immediately and diagnosed our cat soon after.  They walked us through every step, and kept us up to date while our cat stayed a few nights. They even sent us a few pictures.  They made a very difficult time a bit easier.

This is a hard one for me to review.  While they were nice and friendly I took my cat for what I thought was a hurt paw and they couldn’t see anything wrong but decided to do bloodwork and X-rays because he was obviously in pain.  Sadly his heart stopped under sedation and they did preform CPR and while his heart started again he was brain dead so we had to put him down.   They tried to determine what caused this but no answers were found.  I guess I should be pleased they didn’t charge me for all the life saving practices they did.  But still I would pay it all to have my baby back.  Next time my pets need a vet sadly I might think twice especially if sedation is required.  Hug your fur babies tight because you never know how long you have.
Staff is friendly, it’s clean and most of all Amazing vet care for my sick canine.

As soon as we walked in, the receptionists noticed that our elder kitty, Pepper, was panting. Out of an abundance of care, they immediately rushed her to the emergency room to ensure her wellbeing. Luckily, Pepper was okay, and I appreciated their fast reaction and attention to my precious girl. Afterwards, Doctor Farrell took great care of Pepper, who was unfortunately diagnosed with kidney disease. After a very scary night where Pepper was hiding, shaking, vomiting, and refusing food, Dr. Farrell was able to ease our concerns and give us a timeline on her prognosis and quality of life. She prescribed us with some easy to administer medications and gave us some kidney-friendly food for Pepper to enjoy as her disease progresses. (As soon as we got home, Pepper went to town on it!)

The facility was clean and I liked how streamlined their treatment and billing process was. It's pretty much all digital, so you may need a smartphone to access some important documents.

Here was the only unfortunate thing: the entire process took a long time (around 6 hours total). This was for some diagnostics, blood work, and giving her medicine. Granted, this is an emergency hospital, so when a life-or-death emergency is taking place, it makes sense that Pepper might lose priority. But by around 11:30pm with no update, I decided to go in-person to wait. This is when our savior Megan, a doctor's assistant, helped us. We interrupted her in the lobby and asked about Pepper. Even though she wasn't assigned to Pepper, Megan went back and got an update for us from Dr. Farrell and she helped with the discharge by explaining the medication, answering all of our questions, and just generally being so upbeat and compassionate in our time of stress.

Thank you to Dr. Farrell, Megan, and the receptionists at TrueCare for giving my Pepper the love she deserves.

TrueCare has been absolutely wonderful. My Jack Russell has gone to them twice now, as an ER visit (😩)  and they have been nothing but kind & tending to. They saved her little life twice and I could not be more grateful. You can tell they really care about their patients. They called two separate occasions to check in on her as well. Thank you endlessly to the doctors and staff for a better experience while being so stressed and concerned. I highly recommend! Luna is safe and healthy.

Our sweet pup passed away - very suddenly and horrifically - one day after her ER visit with Dr. Nordfeldt. She was an oncology patient at TrueCare and had recently undergone radiation therapy.

During our visit, we specifically begged Dr. Nordfeldt to (1) read her file and (2) inform her oncologist, knowing how critical her recent history was. But it was painfully clear that Dr. Nordfeldt hadn’t even reviewed her medical record - he treated Billie like a brand-new patient. And based on the complete lack of follow-up from anyone on her care team, it seems that communication with her oncologist never happened.

While the outcome may not have changed, what hurts most is the absence of basic dignity and continuity. In such a painful, fragile moment, being met with indifference made the loss even harder. We expected compassion and coordination - not to be left feeling like we had to piece everything together ourselves in her final hours.

She was the best girl and should have been treated with the care she deserved.
Rest in peace, Billie.

I took my Pomeranian in for a vomiting/ throat obstruction concern late evening and the team from start to finish was OUTSTANDING!. From reception & desk assistance to all the Nurse & Doc staff. They were so caring & giving empathy to every owner & pet that walked in. The place is also very clean. The nurses and doctors were thorough with details & instructions. When they brought my dog out and he was wagging his tail in the nurses arms,  I knew instantly he was treated love.
Thank you to this Team & their dedication to our fur babies
-Charlene & Kobe "Montell" Banks

We brought our dog, Ozzie, to TrueCare for Pets late last night.  He got something stuck in his paw on his last walk of the day, and couldn't walk.  They took him back immediately and got it out so fast.  They didn't have to sedate him or keep him long at all.  They moved quickly so they could focus on the more critical dogs.  We were there for less than a 1/2 hour.  The staff was incredible and shout out to GLORIA for loving on our fur baby!!!
Had to euthanize our beloved dog. They were caring... sympathetic... took care of us quickly. Highly recommended.

Dr. Maynard was very caring and provided me with comforting details while she treated my baby Luna. I could tell she was very experienced and trusted every word of advice given to me of how to care for my baby. Wait times are long like every hospital but she made sure to get back to me after following up via phone while waiting on radiology which I really appreciated 🙏🏼 thanks so much!

If you can avoid it, DO NOT COME HERE! Unfortunately my older cat had a seizure at midnight and this was the better reviewed emergency vet. The medical director I saw was nice enough in explaining everything that could be going on with her, as seizures are fairly rare in cats. Without going to neurology, they can't say for sure what would have caused it. That being said, he was pretty sure it wasn't a bacterial infection. I get the estimate back, and it includes a neurological blood panel that's $745. While looking at his screen, I saw that same test listed at $245. He explained it was wholesale vs. retail prices, but come on. $500 difference?? I obviously declined it. She was put on a medication called phenobarbital for what they thought was a grand mal seizure. They recommended an overnight stay, which I was fine with. When I brought her back home, she was pacing and crying all night. I called to ask for advice, and was on the call for a total of 45 minutes while the poor receptionist had to go track down doctors to get the answers to my questions. Instead of showing any amount of concern, they simply told me that her pacing and howling would be a neurological issue and I'd have to go elsewhere to see what's going on. Keep in mind this was INCREDIBLY odd behavior for her, and I pointed out that it only started on this medication. Looking to veterinary articles online, I found out that phenobarbital can cause restlessness and anxiety in dogs. So I called back to let them know that, and they repeated that whatever veterinary guidebook they use did not say that, so it couldn't be true. I was distraught, and at that point looked up if the steroid she was on could have an interaction. Turns out it DOES, so I called back AGAIN and told them that. I still haven't received a call back, but it's insane to me that the vets would not know of this potentially lethal combination.

All of this worry caused me to go and see another vet for a second opinion. He was shocked that they put her on phenobarbital, as the medication is usually used for epileptic animals who have cluster seizures. This was her first seizure, and likely not even a grand mal seizure like TrueCare for pets diagnosed her with. I wish I could give a better rating, because the medical director was very kind. I'm just livid they dismissed my concerns, and it took taking her to another vet to point out their flawed diagnosis.
Absolutely zero compassion! It’s all about the money. I ended up leaving and taking my baby to VCA. Superior service. Showed compassion.
Not good.

Emilie Chaplow internal medicine vet was horrible. Anastasia vets assistance was very helpful and took time to listen and sympathize with us to find better solution.

Vet didnt really consult at all like 15 mins and took $229. Wasted time and money and my poor cat didn’t eat for a day, skipped medication (was instructed to do so) hoping to do some xray.

The reason why I booked the appointment with internal medicine here specifically was to get more info that I couldn’t get from urgent care what is wrong with my cat. So I can avoid expensive urgent care test cost.

Basically all she did was blaming us for not treating my cat from urgent care. It was 8k for treatment, and I couldnt afford. She threw the same 8k bill and left.

Super regret that I had picked here, hope other people know internal medicine vet could not care less than this but still collects full money.

Btw my cat is now fine, met a great vet who TRULY care and did only essential tests based on her pattern and history. And paid 1/3 of quote I got from here.

Unfortunately due to the negligence of this clinic, my dog passed away under their care back in 2021. It has been difficult to think about or share but I feel it’s important for others to know. My little chihuahua was my whole world and my emotional support animal. When she started having emergency symptoms during COVID (bloody diarrhea), I could not find any other emergency vet in our area that had capacity to accept another animal. I brought her to this vet, but after waiting an extremely long amount of time in the car while my dog was very sick, they took her away and told me they would just take her in to run some tests and bring her back out. Because of COVID i was not allowed in with her and never got to say goodbye. They called and said she would need to stay overnight to receive care. I was told hours later that they had done nothing to help her yet, because she was in “stable” condition and other dogs were not. I went to bed and was called during the night to be told they were doing CPR on her and she was coding. I asked them to continue resuscitating  and do whatever it took to help her. Sadly, she never made it out of there alive. I cannot definitively say that they killed her or that their actions directly resulted in her death, however that is how it feels to me. This is a terrible memory and a place that haunts me to this day. I hope changes have been made since then.

Last night was scary! Our dog got a hold of house guests’ THC gummies and started twitching and couldn’t walk straight, if at all. From the moment I called this hospital they were comforting and welcoming. They made everything easy. Once we arrived with Blue they immediately took him in and started observing and running tests. Dr. Farrell was attentive, kind, pro-active and reassuring. She texted me throughout the night, and the same attentive service from Dr. Beyers the following morning. Our fur baby is back to normal, but having this team taking care of him kept us from freaking out. Could not recommend this place enough, GOD forbid you have a pet emergency.
Overpriced and overmedicated.

Broken Promises and Lack of Compassion

Dr. Maya Lottati at TrueCare for Pets initially told me my 14-year-old dog with chronic bronchitis could stay on Hydrocodone “forever.” Later, without warning, she refused to refill it—despite the fact that I never filled the prescription elsewhere due to pharmacy issues.

I’m heartbroken. When it became clear I couldn’t afford a $5,000 surgery, the tone changed, and support disappeared. I was dismissed, blamed, and told not to contact her again.

TrueCare showed me that if you can't afford high-cost treatment, their compassion stops short. Jack deserved better—and so do other pets.

My dog was overdosed on antibiotics and when we took him there and told them multiple times that he was given antibiotics earlier that day which made him sick they still didn’t know what was the reason he got sick. Few hours later my dog’s heart stopped and he died there. Don’t go to them they are only good charging arm and leg, 2k for a diagnose and 5-7K for a treatment.

As a longtime pet owner, this is the best emergency vet ever! I wish they were my regular vet.  We were taken in right away and our beloved dog was given excellent and immediate care.  The vet and staff were compassionate and professional.

Do yourself—and your pet—a favor and avoid this place.
We were warned not to come here, and unfortunately, those warnings proved valid. A last-minute emergency left us with no other option when our dog broke her nail and needed it removed and wrapped. The bandage they applied fell off the very next day due to their poor workmanship. When we went back and asked them to fix their mistake, they refused unless we paid again—charging us twice for a service they failed to do right the first time. This isn’t just unacceptable—it’s unethical. It was never about the money. It was about accountability and basic professionalism, both of which were clearly lacking here.

Really expensive place for them just to give a basic diagnosis and not really recommend anything other than euthanizing your pet or having to pay $7000 to $8000 for the same therapy my family can give him at home. Was recommended some over the counter medicine that cost $12 at CVS but that's about it. Instead of them asking if he had vaccines or any flea treatments in the past they wanted to euthanize him.

Thank you for your review. We truly care about every pet and family we see, and we always want to provide the best experience possible. If there’s anything we could have done differently, we’d love to hear your thoughts. Your feedback helps us grow and improve.

This month, I experienced two heartbreaking losses—my beloved 9-year-old cat Manchas, who passed away from cancer, and my 14-year-old dog Moka, who had battled multiple illnesses over time.

Through it all, the entire team showed me nothing but compassion and kindness. Their humanity and warmth were beyond anything I could have hoped for. I am deeply grateful for the way they cared for my precious fur babies and myself—with both heart and incredible professionalism.

A SPECIAL thank you to Dr. Koo, Ari, Juan, Bryant, Joanne, and  two angels—Dr. Emily Farrel and Sophie. You made both losses as gentle and peaceful as possible, and for that, I will always be thankful.

There are no words to fully express my appreciation for your care and empathy during such a difficult time. Marisol

I had a really great experience here after my dog had a bad reaction to a vaccine. We came in, were seen quickly and he was provided wonderful care at a very reasonable price. The coffee machine and comfortable couches in the waiting room make the nervous waiting process more comfortable/tolerable. Every person who works here that I interacted with was wonderful. I am recommending this place to all of my friends who have pets in case of an emergency.

Absolutely the best care. Compassionate and went above and beyond when we had to put our boy to sleep.  The extra kindness was Absolutely appreciated. Fur baby girl had surgery there last year. Excellent care as well. I can't fault them for a single thing and would Absolutely recommend them.

Come here if you want a uncomfortable chair for 12 hours of your life waiting fpr simple procedure for your animal while staff's only answer is "Oh , they are short staffed in the back" while three receptionists laugh in the front doing nothing.

TrueCare is great. Our dog was sick on a Saturday night and our regular vet was closed. We called TrueCare, explained her symptoms, and they advised us to come in to get her checked out. We checked in online, and when we arrived they took our dog in quickly. The vet was very kind and great at explaining the issues to us. We received a text message with her discharge instructions and all medications we would need. We're very grateful for them, as our dog is very old and needed medical attention right away. Dr. Norfeldt and all staff members were very nice, helpful, and calm. The building was very comfortable and clean as well. If you need a 24 hour emergency vet, TrueCare is the place!
They treated my dog as transactional instead of family
Terrible place terrible vets ,price higher than here u cant in the world..not reccomend at all

I felt compelled to write this review, even though it won't bring my dog back to life. In October 2024, I took my dog, Annie Matzoball, to the vet next door to Truecare for Pets because she was vomiting and not feeling well. After an X-ray, they suggested that she likely had a tumor and recommended that I find a specialist and take her to an emergency clinic to determine the best course of action.

This was during the week of Halloween, and it was a Friday night. Annie spent the whole day at their facility, and I received numerous emails, texts, and calls about the next steps. To summarize, my dog underwent a blood test, ultrasound, and various other procedures. I expected to pick her up around 8 or 9 PM, but I didn't leave until after 12:30 AM.

During a conversation around 12:30-12:45, they suggested that I let her stay overnight for IV hydration. I declined, stating that she would be better off sleeping at home with me than in a cage overnight. So I picked up Annie around 1 AM and left the clinic.

A month later, I learned that Annie had cancer. I have been grappling with this information ever since. I believe that if she had received proper care and discharge from Truecare for Pets, I could have provided her with a better quality of life for her remaining time.

I feel furious but understand that life goes on.
The worst place. They are incompetent

I brought my dog in for a quick check and staff was amazing. The guy below was in the waiting room (Amir Farrahi) and was screaming at the staff and acting like a child. His review is baseless and he seemed more concerned about leaving the vet than the status of his pet.
Bunch of time wasters!!! Avoid this vet if you have an emergency! They don't seem to understand the urgency or importance of handling critical cases promptly.

TrueCare for pets saved my chihuahua life. Dr. Sibrian was amazing! The staff at true care for pets are friendly and helpful. I normally never give feedback unless it was a great experience. Truecare for pets left the biggest impact on me. I will forever be grateful to them for saving my dog. Thank you so much!

I just had to take my dog in for a serious emergency, they immediately took her back and started working on her. She was in congestive heart failure and trouble breathing. They immediately gave her medicine and oxygen. So happy I took her to this vet, they are so amazing, caring and patient! Thank you for saving my fur baby. I am forever grateful!
Just go to any VCA or Access. One star experience. They will tell you any scary things to squeeze money out of you

Thank you for saving my cat. This vet hospital is incredibly thoughtful and kind. They answer my questions clearly and explain everything about care very well. They were helpful with advice. My cat came home after a hospitalization here, and I was nervous about a behaviour at about 3:00 am. I sent a text at 3:15 to the team and got an answer back at 3:20. I cant reccomend them enough.

If you care for your pets health at all DO NOT GO HERE. We went to this emergency vet when my fiance's cat threw up white foam out of nowhere and were concerned we took her in around 8:40pm. They took her cat and "performed an exam" and then told us it would be a 2-4hr wait to talk to a vet about her exam. After getting her cat back after the exam we were put in a waiting room we were forgotten about for 4 hours and heard the techs and receptionists asking eachother where my fiances cat was and we had to inform them that we had been waiting in the room they put us in... after finally getting a vet tech to talk to us we were condescending and tried to convince us to pay $1300 before the vet actually talked to us and then found out that the vet needed to actually perform an exam. After the vet finally came to us to speak with us after waiting for over 5hrs at that point and my fiances cat had been fine while waiting we were further condescended to by the vet and talked to like we were children, and then gave us food samples for a "bland" diet to help and the food they gave us food that has been recalled multiple times for poisoning animals in last few years. DO NOT GO HERE they are a racket and are just trying to take advantage of your anxiety and panic to get you to pay before you ever even have your animal looked at. Hands down worst experience I've ever had at an emergency vet in my life. And that's saying something considering I've had dogs, cats, and horses my entire life.

I was able to get my husky, Bandit, in super fast after he had an allergy attack; the team here are extremely sweet, knowledgeable, and kind. Dani / the whole staff really lead with compassion, care, and love. We were so happy we got to come here and work with them and we look forward to coming back!!

Extremely compassionate veterinary practice!  From the first phone call to the follow up from ER surgery - we felt like part of the family.  Highly recommend for their care, professionalism, kindness and cleanliness

This place will always stay close with my heart. I had to put down my 13 year old German shepherd (Archie) and I was treated with such dignity and respect. I was such a mess I could barely talk in the lobby, without having to ask the staff offered me a private area to grieve/fill out forms. If you are in need of a vet that’s 24 hours I recommend this place.

Our english bulldog started urinating blood on Thanksgiving morning. Her regular vet wasn't open so we rushed her here. They saw her quickly and treated her so well. Dr. Maynard explained what each procedure was and gave us meds for her UTI. As far as emergency pet care on a holiday goes- I felt like the pricing was honest and fair.

Brought my elderly dog in after a couple of days of bloody stool and though they were very busy, they saw her quickly. I wish someone would have communicated what was going on when they whisked her away for 4-ish hours, but when I finally saw a doctor, she was incredibly kind and caring and comforting.

A nightmare from the movies and my dog wasn’t even seen by a doctor. Came in because my small dog’s eye was bleeding.  Checked in and sat down with my dog, was told to wait for a technician. While sitting with my dog in the waiting area, one of their customers passed by like he owns the place and literally hits my dog in the face with his huge calf on the bloody eye side and she screamed. I was in shock, she just got hurt at this veterinary facility!! I came here to get her help not to make her issue even worse!       Plus the space for him to walk was so big!! Why did he choose to walk so close to her, we’re in urgent care for pets for dog’s sake!! Stay far away from the dog! Well, none of the staff stood up for me when I gasped and told them what happened, not even a “watch where you’re walking sir!”. I felt so helpless that I started crying and having a panic attack. My dog’s EYE WAS BLEEDING and she pretty much just GOT KICKED IN THE FACE in this facility by a trashy man with no respect for small animals or self awareness - not even an apology or remorse. Beware of the type of people who come here, your fur baby might not even be safe. Anyways, so I sat and waited for 2 hours and then finally another vet took over for the original vet assigned to us because they were leaving, and just told me “her eye is no longer bleeding, the vet thinks you can take her home”. Couldn’t that have been established an hour prior to? Of course, we were so happy to just get out of there and didn’t question the offer too much. Will go see someone else elsewhere today, where she won’t get kicked in the face. Two stars because the staff were nice to the customers and the pets overall.. but maybe too nice?

I accidently hit my cat while entering my driveway very slowly late at night.  He seemed to be in shock and I could not tell where he was hit at.  When I brought him to TruCare I was told that I needed to pony up a $2K deposit.  I did it on CareCredit thankfully.  I was told that would be for a diagnostic which I was strongly encouraged was needed.  I really did not believe the final cost would be nearly that amount. But it was already one in the morning and I had no idea whether the poor cat was very injured.  Anyway after tons of x-rays which alone were about $700 and other unjustified charges, I got my cat out of there with a diagnosis of having just the hair on his tail get caught beneath my tire.  There was a pull on the tail which resulted in him having a tiny bit of difficulty walking but overall nothing was really wrong.  A total of $1700 were the final charges.  I basically spent the night there because no one ever came out to talk to me the entire night until I initiated it, which I had to do 3 times.  They would have been fine with me sleeping on their couches and never coming to tell my about my cat as long as they could charge me.  I wish there were other emergency vets around.  This one is clearly in the money making business.

Besides everyone else that works there, they seemed very nice and understanding but this awful lady named VADA. I took my cat in because I had concerns that he was having a blockage.
